Rust Titan Exchange WebSocket client/CLI: streaming quotes, one-shot prices, reconnect/backoff, queued streams, Solana instructions. See `FOR_USER.md` for architecture/pitfalls.

Commands:
`cargo build --release`
`cargo run --features cli --bin titan-cli -- --help`
`cargo run --features cli --bin titan-cli -- info`
`cargo run --features cli --bin titan-cli -- price SOL USDC 1000000000`
`cargo run --features cli --bin titan-cli -- stream SOL USDC 1000000000`
`cargo run --features cli --bin titan-cli -- swap --keypair ~/.config/solana/id.json SOL USDC 100000000`
`cargo run --features cli --bin titan-cli -- watch`
`cargo test --test [name]`
`cargo clippy --all-targets`

Stream slots use `active_count` and `Arc<AtomicBool>` so exactly one stop/end/failure path releases each slot; `on_end` bridges connection and queue accounting. Reconnection updates `effective_stream_id` for `StopStream`. Initial quote frames may be empty; don’t assert nonempty unless using a real wallet.

Style: **Maximum file size: ~200 lines** - Split larger files
**mod.rs files should be empty** - Only contain mod declarations, move content to meaningful file names
Use helper structs with static methods. Single `TitanClientError`; all fallible operations return `Result`. **Never panic** - Always propagate errors via Result
Use native `async fn`; no boxed futures or `async-trait` unless necessary. Tokio-only; use `pub` everywhere. Instrument public methods with `#[tracing::instrument(skip_all)]`. **No inline log statements**; remove `println!`, `dbg!`, and most `tracing::info!`; keep only `tracing::error!` and `tracing::warn!` for critical issues. Minimal docs; centralize constants, avoid magic numbers, re-export `titan-api-types` directly.
